anchor.quote: Implement the three methods by issuing per-item requests in parallel (Promise.all), honouring meta.headers and meta.method the same way the single-item methods do.

behaviours: The return type of dataProvider(apiUrl, httpClient, options) in packages/simple-rest/src/provider.ts is Required<DataProvider>. It no longer omits "createMany" | "updateMany" | "deleteMany".

createMany({ resource, variables: [a, b], meta }) sends one request per item to `${apiUrl}/${resource}`, all in parallel through Promise.all. The default method is "post" and the item is the request body. It resolves to { data: [responseA, responseB] }, in the same order as the input.

updateMany({ resource, ids: [1, 2], variables, meta }) sends one request per id to `${apiUrl}/${resource}/${id}`, all in parallel through Promise.all. The default method is "patch" and variables is the request body. It resolves to { data: [response1, response2] }, in the same order as ids.

deleteMany({ resource, ids: [1, 2], variables, meta }) sends one request per id to `${apiUrl}/${resource}/${id}`, all in parallel through Promise.all. The default method is "delete" and variables is sent as the axios `data` config. It resolves to { data: [response1, response2] }, in the same order as ids.
When meta.headers is set, every per-item request made by createMany, updateMany and deleteMany sends those headers, just as create, update and deleteOne do.
When meta.method is set (for example "put" for updateMany or "patch" for createMany), every per-item request uses that HTTP method instead of the default, just as create, update and deleteOne do.

Partial failure: if one per-item request fails (for example a 500 or 404 for one id) while the others succeed, createMany, updateMany and deleteMany reject with that request's error. They do not resolve with partial data. Each method has at least one test for this case.
Calling createMany with an empty variables array, or updateMany or deleteMany with an empty ids array, sends no requests and resolves to { data: [] }.
Behaviour of getList, getMany, create, update, getOne, deleteOne, getApiUrl and custom is unchanged. All existing @refinedev/simple-rest tests pass with no changes to their expected results.

With the provider methods present, @refinedev/core's useCreateMany, useUpdateMany and useDeleteMany call the provider's createMany, updateMany and deleteMany instead of falling back to per-item create, update and deleteOne.

documentation/docs/data/packages/simple-rest/index.md documents createMany, updateMany and deleteMany. It says they issue parallel per-item requests, explains the meta.headers and meta.method support, and describes what happens when one item fails.
A changeset file .changeset/simple-rest-bulk-methods.md marks a minor bump for @refinedev/simple-rest and describes the new bulk methods.
modules.name: simple-rest bulk methods

questions.affects: What useCreateMany, useUpdateMany and useDeleteMany show the user when one item in a bulk action fails (error notification versus partial success), and what the required partial-failure test asserts.
questions.if_wrong: With reject-all, records that were written or deleted on the server look like failures in the UI and are not invalidated, so lists show stale data and users may retry and create duplicates. With resolve-partial, a real failure can be hidden as a success.
questions.q: On partial failure (some per-item requests succeed and one fails), should createMany, updateMany and deleteMany reject the whole call with the first error (plain Promise.all), or resolve with the items that succeeded and report which ones failed (for example with Promise.allSettled)?

questions.affects: Which test files and test infrastructure the unit must add, and how QA decides whether that acceptance criterion is met.
questions.if_wrong: If a live json-server test is required but only mocks are written, the criterion is unproven at review. If mocks are enough but a live server is set up, the unit adds infrastructure and flaky network tests outside its scope.
questions.q: The acceptance criterion says 'work against json-server'. Is it enough to prove this with nock-mocked unit tests in packages/simple-rest/test (as the existing create, update and deleteOne tests do against https://api.fake-rest.refine.dev), or is an integration test against a running json-server instance required?

questions.affects: How many HTTP requests hit the API at once when users bulk-edit or bulk-delete many rows.
questions.if_wrong: Unbounded parallel requests on large selections can trip rate limits or overload the backend, causing the partial failures described above. Adding a limit when none is wanted makes bulk actions slower and the code more complex than asked.
questions.q: Should the bulk methods send every per-item request at once (unbounded Promise.all, as the ticket says), or limit how many requests run concurrently for large id lists?

sealed_acceptance_criteria.text: Provider return type no longer omits these methods.
useCreateMany / useUpdateMany / useDeleteMany work against json-server.
Tests for each method, including one partial-failure case.
simple-rest docs page under documentation/ updated.
